coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (in the order requested):
1. Wikipedia "2008 Florida Gators football team" — has a real "Coaching staff" table (section 6.3) listing the head coach plus 9 on-field assistants. Note: the WebFetch/markdown rendering of this page sometimes drops that table; it is present in the article HTML and in the wikitext (Special:Export). Its own citation points at a July 2009 Wayback capture of gatorzone.com/football/bios.php, which is the 2009 staff, NOT 2008 — I did not rely on that capture.
2. School athletics site archived near the title date — https://web.archive.org/web/20081217012732/http://www.gatorzone.com/football/bios.php (captured Dec 17, 2008, i.e. between the SEC title game and the Jan 8, 2009 BCS Championship). Its "Coaches" block confirms all 10 on-field coaches and exactly one support-staff name (Terry Jackson). Note for the verifier: on this page the coach NAME and the ROLE sit in two separate <td> cells, so no single verbatim run contains both. I therefore quoted the contiguous role string only from this source, and used Wikipedia (where name and role are one contiguous list item) for name+role quotes.
3. 2008 Florida football media guide — this is where essentially all support-staff coverage comes from. The linked floridagators.com URL (/documents/2016/2/11/2008_FB_media_guide.pdf?id=14741) returns an HTML wrapper page, not the PDF; the actual file is the S3 URL I cited (110 MB, 208 pages). Support staff bios are on printed pp. 88-92, the "Football Staff" photo grid + "2008 Athletic Trainers" + "2008 Managers" lists on printed p. 92, the "2008 Sports Health Staff" grid on printed p. 22, and a compact staff directory in "2008 Florida Football Quick Facts" on printed p. 205.

QUOTE HONESTY: Per the instructions, every media-guide row has quote set to "" because the PDF's text layer does not extract faithfully — it injects spurious intra-word spaces (the extracted text literally reads "Anthony P ass", "Mark P antoni", "Ky l e  J o h n s t o n", "Human P erformance"). Any mechanical string match would fail through no fault of the claim. Each of those rows instead carries a note with the exact printed page and the exact printed wording of the name/title block. Rows sourced from Wikipedia and the Wayback gatorzone capture DO carry true verbatim quotes.

WHAT I RECOVERED
- On-field: complete. All 10 (head coach + 9 assistants), triple-sourced (Wikipedia table, Dec-2008 gatorzone capture, media guide Quick Facts p. 205).
- Strength & conditioning: 4 (Marotti, Holsopple, Campbell, Piraino), all with full media-guide bios.
- Graduate assistants: 2 (Sean Cronin - defense, Zach Smith - offense), both with full media-guide bios.
- Operations/personnel/recruiting/video/academic: 12, from media-guide bios, the p. 92 "Football Staff" grid, and the p. 205 directory.
- Equipment: 2 (Baisden, McGrew).
- Medical/sports health/nutrition: 18, including the football-specific athletic training staff, the physicians/dentists/therapists on the p. 92 "Football Staff" grid, and the graduate interns and athletic training students named on p. 92.
- Student managers: 10, named on p. 92 under "2008 Managers / Student Assistants".

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER / CAVEATS
- ANALYST tier: nothing. Florida in 2008 had no documented "analyst" titles; that role category did not exist in the program's published materials for this era. Zero rows returned as analyst — this is a genuine absence, not a research gap.
- QUALITY CONTROL tier: no 2008 QC staffer is documented anywhere I could find. The only QC mention in the guide is retrospective — Zach Smith's bio says he held a "Special Teams and Offensive Quality Control" role in 2006 before becoming a GA. If Florida employed QC assistants in 2008 they were not published. Zero qc rows.
- GA count: only 2 GAs are documented. NCAA rules of the era permitted up to 4 football GAs, so it is likely 1-2 more existed and were simply not printed in the media guide. I did not guess at names.
- The media guide went to press in June 2008 (InDesign stamps read 6/14/08 and 6/15/08). It therefore reflects the roster of support staff at the START of the season. I cross-checked the on-field staff against the December 2008 capture and they match exactly, but I have NO independent December/January confirmation for any support-staff row. Anyone in the support tiers who left between June 2008 and the Jan 8, 2009 title game would not be flagged here — I could not find a late-season staff directory to check against.
- SCOPE JUDGMENT: I included the p. 22 "2008 Sports Health Staff" grid (Chris Patrick, Dr. Jay Clugston, Tim Shay, Susan Tillman, Anna Grout, Joshua Chatman) even though some are University Athletic Association department-wide rather than football-only, because that page appears inside the football media guide. Ring-eligibility for these is a judgment call for the dataset owner. Similarly, Ross DeWitt (Director of Aviation) and Malcom Jowers (Team Security) appear on the football staff page but are department resources.
- I deliberately EXCLUDED the Sports Information / media relations staff (Steve McClain, Mary Howard, etc., printed p. 206-207) — they are athletic department SID, not football staff.
- Hiram de Fries is listed on p. 92 with the literal title "Football Staff" (verified via layout-mode extraction, so it is his title and not a stray section header). His actual function — Meyer's longtime mentor/advisor — is not stated in the guide, so I recorded the title as printed and categorized him "other".
- Two names in the p. 92 manager list appear to contain typos in the source ("Evan Hillestsad", "Alexis Candelania"). I reproduced them exactly as printed rather than correcting them.
- MIDSEASON: two flagged. Dan Mullen accepted the Mississippi State head job in December 2008 but coached the BCS title game; Steve Addazio was promoted to offensive coordinator on Dec 27, 2008, before the Jan 8 title game. Both were on staff at the championship game, so both count under the ring rule. Vance Bedford, Kenny Carter and Dan McCarney were all first-year hires who arrived in the 2008 offseason (replacing Doc Holliday, Stan Drayton and Greg Mattison), not mid-season arrivals, so they carry no midseason_note.
